tagline.text: A southern Panay heritage walk linking a battle-relief church and hillside Campo Santo

location.label: Location

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day in town; a day with Iloilo transfers and a Miagao stop

children.text: San Joaquin in southern Iloilo pairs a church’s battle relief with Campo Santo’s stone gateway and staircase. Add the town plaza, a meal and bandi peanut brittle between the two heritage sites. The church and cemetery occupy separate locations, with worship, remembrance and current access shaping the visit.

San Joaquin suits a journey along Iloilo’s southern coast. Look beyond a quick facade photograph to the subject of its carvings and the spatial arrangement of the separate Campo Santo. The pace is that of observing stone and brick detail, then using the town’s plaza and food stops, rather than a shopping or island-hopping day.

The parish church and cemetery chapel are different buildings. The representative pin marks the town-centre church; Campo Santo requires its own entrance and road approach. Miagao Church and Garin Farm are separate stops too. Centre the programme on the two heritage sites before adding other venues around weather and return transport.

Both places retain a purpose beyond sightseeing. The church serves worshippers and the cemetery receives families remembering relatives. An open gate does not automatically permit entry to the sanctuary or chapel. The cemetery gateway, steps and exterior provide architectural interest when an interior is unavailable.

Study the overlapping soldiers, horses and movement across the triangular pediment. The scene concerns Spanish and Moroccan forces at Tétouan in Morocco, rather than a Philippine battle. Read the NHCP history before considering this military image within colonial religious architecture, observing the relief without touching it or climbing closer.

blocks.title: Pause inside the church when permitted

children.text: When visitor access is permitted, look quietly from the entrance along the nave toward the altar. Compare that extended interior with the busy exterior relief. Wait outside during services or ceremonies and ask about photography. The interior gallery records 2023, with current decoration and access checked separately.

blocks.title: Follow Campo Santo’s gateway and stairs

children.text: Align the entrance arch with the chapel above the steps, then look more closely at carved foliage, brick and the dome. The elevated approach feels different from the parish church. Chapel access is not promised; avoid wet steps and restricted areas.

blocks.title: See the plaza and everyday town life

children.text: Take a break around the church plaza, public buildings and small shops. Signs and decorative features provide a backdrop while the area remains a place for everyday movement and community events. The town is worth observing without expecting a festival or parade.

blocks.title: Treat a coastal stop as an optional extension

children.text: With time available, consider a coast location with confirmed access. A resort outside the centre needs its own transfer and conditions. The Ember Beach image records that coastal venue in 2018; it does not promise the same facilities, free entry or swimming today. Check separate access and safety arrangements for any water activity.

Bandi, made with peanuts and caramelized sugar, adds a small local-food stop. Compare size, ingredients and packaging before choosing quantities. Avoid it with a peanut allergy and check sealing and storage for gifts. The photograph does not establish current price, brand availability or stock.

Establish the return pickup after arriving near the church. Read the NHCP history and observe the pediment. Enter briefly when permitted, or continue to the plaza after an exterior visit if a ceremony or closure prevents entry.

Rest near the plaza and check a meal’s menu and ordering time. Inspect ingredients and packaging when buying bandi. Arrange the Campo Santo transfer and return before leaving rather than searching urgently for a ride by the cemetery road.

items.time: Later · Campo Santo exterior and return

children.text: Check access and mourners’ movements, then observe the arch, stairs and chapel. Stay below for an overview if the steps are difficult. Keep out of the carriageway for photographs and finish in time for the agreed return transport.

items.time: Morning · Transfer and first heritage stop

children.text: Choose the order of Miagao and San Joaquin around transport and access. Read the different relief subjects instead of treating the facades as interchangeable photographs. If one visit takes longer, shorten the next to preserve the return margin.

items.time: Afternoon · Campo Santo and an optional stop

children.text: After the second church and Campo Santo, use remaining time for rest or a snack. Garin Farm or a coastal resort requires a separate visit and transfer, so neither is essential to this heritage day. Prioritize terminal or airport requirements when travelling onward.

These are personal itinerary ideas, not a tour timetable. Adjust the order around ceremonies, remembrance, rain and actual transport. Respecting access and allowing time home matters more than completing a long venue list.

For public transport, verify the current southern departure point and San Joaquin destination. Jeepney boarding and the separate bus facilities around Mohon should not be assumed to share one building. Check the chosen operator’s departure and return arrangements rather than travelling solely by an old Molo terminal name. Blog guides (2018 and 2024) put the bus or jeepney ride at roughly 1.5–2 hours and the fare at about ₱60–100, but they disagree on the boarding point (Molo vs Mohon) and the amount, so confirm locally.

With a hired vehicle, list the church and Campo Santo separately and agree on waiting, return and extra stops. Check inclusions such as fuel, parking and overtime before dividing a day-hire cost. Use the precise drop-off rather than a general town-entry point.

items.title: Connecting from the airport or port

children.text: Count arrival procedures, luggage and transfers before heading south from the airport or port. San Joaquin is a separate provincial journey rather than a central-city church stop. After a late arrival, compare an overnight city stay and daylight visit the next day.

On the final travel day, plan around actual return boarding rather than merely the end of sightseeing. Reduce extra coastal stops or shopping if rain or transfers delay the journey. Arrange luggage storage elsewhere rather than assuming the church or cemetery provides it.

items.title: Between the church and Campo Santo

children.text: A separate road segment links the sites. Assess pavements, crossings and heat before choosing to walk, or compare local transport. Keep off traffic lanes and do not turn away from approaching vehicles for photographs. Retain a lower-level exterior option at Campo Santo for visitors who find stairs difficult.

Plan exposed heritage walks in daylight during relatively dry conditions. Morning or late afternoon may be more comfortable than midday, subject to church access and ceremonies. A dusk photograph does not establish night visiting hours at Campo Santo. Finish steps and road transfers before darkness.

No current official visitor-hours or admission table was verified, so continuous or free access is not promised. Follow the day’s parish and cemetery guidance. Worship and family remembrance take priority during Holy Week and cemetery observances.

per person for a day. Add private hire, a coastal venue or Garin Farm separately. Distinguish parish or cemetery donation guidance from other activity admission and pay only clearly identified charges. Carry suitable small cash for meals and minor purchases.

An Iloilo base can suit a return heritage day. For a longer southern-coast or Antique journey, choose accommodation around the next destination and transport. Check a coastal property’s actual position and evening food and transfer arrangements rather than assuming a walk to the church.

Use lunch as a proper break between heritage sites. Choose suitable food after checking the menu and preparation, with drinking water available. Keep meals and alcohol out of the cemetery. Allow alternatives as businesses around either site can change after photographs were taken.

Bandi is brittle, so consider packaging and the remaining journey. Check ingredients, expiry and sealing for gifts, protecting it from pressure in the bag. Keep food separate from wet items after a coastal stop and verify any private resort’s current operation and access terms.
Save the church and Campo Santo as separate destinations and check both approaches before departure.

Respect the cemetery’s commemorative purpose and obtain appropriate consent for filming families or using a drone.
Check wet stone and exposed paving, using a lower-level exterior visit when steps are slippery.
Distinguish dated photographs from the belfry’s current form and access controls, without assuming an unverified reason for changes.
